title: People’s Mañanera September 29
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**From the Home to Universal Health Care  
** The "House-to-House Healthcare" program has provided 24.8 million
consultations and is helping 818,000 patients with chronic conditions manage
their health. In addition, a network of 12,750 clinics is being established,
and starting in January, the exchange of services between healthcare
institutions will begin.

**Public Health Is Regaining Its Capacity  
** In two years, 33 hospitals were opened, and over 3.18 billion doses of
medications and medical supplies were delivered. The Mexican Social Security
Institute (IMSS) added 32,000 employees to its rolls; IMSS-Bienestar will
provide more than 60 million consultations, and the number of surgeries will
have increased by 25%. President Claudia Sheinbaum explained that "we are now
reversing 36 years of neglect and moving forward."

**Mexico Defends Its Interests in the USMCA  
** Mexico is maintaining its dialogue with the U.S. government to avoid new
tariffs and reduce those applied to steel, aluminum, and automobiles.
Sheinbaum noted that no agreement has been finalized yet but added that "we
are interested in economic integration, but always with (respect for national)
sovereignty."

**Ayotzinapa: The Investigation Remains Open  
** Twelve years after the forced disappearance of the 43 Ayotzinapa teacher
training college students, new leads have identified 17 individuals under
investigation, and 30 new suspects have been arrested, according to the
government. The President reiterated that "we will not stop investigating
until justice is served and we find the (missing) young people."

**There Is No "Anti-Meme Law"  
**Sheinbaum dismissed the notion that the anti-piracy reform seeks to ban
memes or limit what is posted on social media. Rather, it aims to combat
piracy and the improper commercial use of official symbols. She clarified that
the reform seeks to prevent the private commercialization of official symbols.
